title: How Much You Should Save Before Taking an International Trip
description: Budgeting for the 'Trip of a Lifetime' without credit card debt.
content:
International travel is a major life goal for many, but the price tag can be deceptive. A '$500 flight' to Europe is just the beginning. Between lodging, food, currency conversion fees, and local transport, a 10-day trip can easily cost $3,000-$5,000 per person. Many travelers return home to find they spent double their budget. To enjoy the trip without financial anxiety, you need a fully funded 'Travel Wallet' before you board the plane. This guide breaks down the hidden costs of international travel.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Daily Burn' Rate: Estimate your daily spend (Hotel + Food + Activities). For Western Europe/Japan, budget $250/day per person. For Southeast Asia/Latin America, budget $100/day.
  • The 'Pre-Trip' Costs: Passports ($130), Luggage, Vaccinations, and Travel Insurance often add $500 before you leave the country.
  • Currency Buffer: Exchange rates fluctuate. Add a 10% buffer to your savings goal in case the dollar weakens while you are there.
  • Re-Entry Fund: You need money for the Uber home from the airport and groceries the next day. Don't come home to $0.

Why It Matters (US Context)

US credit cards often charge 'Foreign Transaction Fees' (3%). Ensure you get a card with 0% foreign fees (like Capital One or Chase Sapphire) before you go. Saving 3% on a $5,000 trip puts $150 back in your pocket.

The Trip Calculator

Scenario: 10 Days in Italy (Couple).

1. Fixed Costs (Booked Ahead)

  • Flights: $2,000 (Economy).
  • Hotels/AirBnB: $2,500 ($250/night).
  • Trains/Transit Pass: $400.
  • Subtotal: $4,900.

2. Variable Costs (Spending Money)

  • Food: $1,500 ($150/day for two).
  • Tours/Museums: $500.
  • Shopping/Souvenirs: $300.
  • Subtotal: $2,300.

3. The Target

Total: $7,200.
To save this in 1 year, you need $600/month.

Savings & Spend Strategy

  1. Open a 'Trip Fund': Use a High-Yield Savings Account. Automate the $600/mo transfer. Do not book the flight until you have at least 50% saved.
  2. Points Redemption: Use credit card points for the Flights/Hotels. This reduces the 'Fixed Cost' bucket, leaving your cash for food and fun.
  3. ATM Strategy: Don't exchange cash at the airport (bad rates). Use a Schwab Investor Checking card at a local ATM in the destination country to get the best rate with $0 fees.
  4. VAT Refund: In Europe, you can get ~12% sales tax back on large purchases. Save your receipts and process the refund at the airport. It's free money.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is travel insurance worth it?

Yes. Medical evacuations can cost $50,000. A $50 policy is cheap protection. Check if your credit card already includes it.

Should I use cash or card?

Card for everything possible (better exchange rate). Cash for small street vendors. Always select 'Pay in Local Currency' on the card terminal to avoid dynamic currency conversion fees.

How do I save faster?

Cut dining out at home. 'Eat cheap now to eat well in Rome.' Visualize the trade-off.
